binders: There exist real constants c and C, chosen before all subsequent data.
Universally quantified types ι and Ω are equipped respectively with a finite-type structure and a measurable-space structure.
μ is an implicit measure on Ω equipped with an IsProbabilityMeasure instance.
X is an implicit family X : ι → Ω → ℝ, and hne proves that the universal finite set of indices is nonempty.
After the family assumptions, λ is an arbitrary implicit real number.
For the conclusion, i ranges over every element of ι.
hypotheses: Every component X i is measurable.
Every component X i is μ-integrable and has mean zero: ∫ X i dμ = 0.
Every component gauge LocalDef002 μ (X i) is strictly below ∞.
The indexed family X is jointly independent under μ.
Writing K = max over i of (LocalDef002 μ (X i)).toReal, the parameter satisfies |λ| K ≤ c.
conclusions: For every i, the function ω ↦ exp(λ X i ω) is μ-integrable.
For every i, ∫ exp(λ X i) dμ ≤ exp(C λ² ((LocalDef002 μ (X i)).toReal)²).
mathematical_definitions: A scale t ∈ ENNReal is admissible for X under μ precisely when X is measurable, t ≠ 0, t ≠ ∞, ω ↦ exp(|X(ω)|/t.toReal) is μ-integrable, and its integral is at most 2.
LocalDef002 μ X is the ENNReal infimum of all admissible scales t.
K is the finite maximum over all indices i of the real conversions of the component gauges.
translation.proposition_plain_english: There are universal positive real constants c and C such that, for every nonempty finite jointly independent family of measurable, integrable, mean-zero real random variables on a probability space whose exponential-moment gauges are finite, every real λ in the common window |λ| max_i gauge(X_i) ≤ c gives, component by component, an integrable moment-generating function satisfying E[exp(λX_i)] ≤ exp(C λ² gauge(X_i)²). The gauge is the infimum of nonzero finite scales t for which E[exp(|X|/t)] ≤ 2, with integrability explicitly required.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The index type must be finite and nonempty; empty families are excluded.
The measure must be a probability measure.
Each component must separately be measurable, integrable, centered, and have finite gauge.
The constants c and C are existential and universal across all later choices, but their numerical values are unspecified.
The effective window is non-strict and symmetric in λ because it is |λ|K ≤ c; λ itself may be positive, zero, or negative.
The maximum gauge K controls the allowed λ, whereas the right-hand side uses the individual component's gauge.
If K = 0, the window condition admits every real λ; the proposition contains no explicit separate treatment of this case.
The gauge is an infimum and need not be attained by an admissible scale.
Admissible scales explicitly exclude both 0 and ∞ and require integrability in addition to the integral bound.
Because the family conditions and window are antecedents of implications, the assertion is vacuous for data that fail any antecedent.
